# monthend-report-demo

Turns messy accounting CSV exports into a clean **month-end Excel workbook** and a **one-page PDF summary**: actual vs budget, change vs last month, by category and by department, with a log of every line that was fixed, removed or flagged.

**All data here is synthetic.** "Example Co.", its vendors and every amount are generated by [`src/sample.js`](src/sample.js). No client data is in this repo.

**See the output without running anything:**
[`output/monthend-2026-10.pdf`](output/monthend-2026-10.pdf) · [`output/monthend-2026-10.xlsx`](output/monthend-2026-10.xlsx) · [messy input](data/raw/ledger_export_2026-10.csv)

## What goes in

Two monthly ledger exports (Sep and Oct 2026) of the kind accounting tools and banks produce, with the usual problems:

```csv
TXN-202610-0001,2026-10-01,Ridgeline Property Mgmt ,admin,RENT,"$14,500.00","Office lease, Unit 4"
TXN-202610-0002,1-Oct-2026,Signal Ad Co,Administration,Marketing,1816.97,
TXN-202610-0003,10/01/2026,SIGNAL AD CO,Administration,MARKETING,2928.96,"Monthly, see PO"
TXN-202610-0009, 2026/10/05 ,Quillfield Design,it,Contractors,3404.47,
```

| Problem in the export | What the cleaner does |
|---|---|
| Four date formats (`2026-10-01`, `10/01/2026`, `1-Oct-2026`, ` 2026/10/05 `) | Normalised to ISO dates; impossible dates (`31/31/2026`) excluded and flagged |
| `$1,234.50`, `1234.5`, `(45.00)`, `-$45.00` | Parsed to exact cents; bracketed amounts treated as credits |
| `Ops`, `OPS`, `operations `, `I.T.`, `Administration` | Mapped to four standard departments |
| `RENT`, `software`, `Office Supplies ` | Matched to the standard category list |
| `SIGNAL AD CO` vs `Signal Ad Co` | Matched against a vendor master list ([`data/vendors.csv`](data/vendors.csv)) |
| Lines exported twice | Removed, logged against the line they duplicate |
| Same Txn ID with different details | Excluded and flagged for follow-up, never silently merged |
| Blank rows, repeated header at a page break, `TOTAL` footer | Skipped and logged |
| Missing amount | Excluded and flagged for follow-up |

Nothing is dropped silently. Every skipped line appears on the **Data Issues** tab with its file, line number and original text.

## What comes out

**Excel workbook** ([`output/monthend-2026-10.xlsx`](output/monthend-2026-10.xlsx))

- **Summary**: total spend, budget, variance, change vs prior month, categories more than 10% over budget, top vendors, cleaning counts
- **By Category** and **By Department**: budget, actual, over/(under) in $ and %, prior month, change. Variance and total columns are live Excel formulas, so editing a budget figure updates the sheet; over-budget cells are highlighted
- **Transactions**: every clean transaction, filterable, with its source file
- **Data Issues**: every line that was skipped or excluded, and why

**PDF one-pager** ([`output/monthend-2026-10.pdf`](output/monthend-2026-10.pdf)): KPI tiles, actual vs budget chart, department table and plain-English notes for someone who won't open the workbook.

## How the numbers are checked

The sample generator builds a clean "source of truth" ledger first and then makes it messy. The tests ([`test/clean.test.js`](test/clean.test.js)) clean the messy export and check that:

- every real transaction is recovered exactly once, with the right date, vendor, department, category and amount
- the cleaned total matches the source of truth **to the cent**
- each injected problem (duplicates, blank rows, page-break headers, footers, missing amounts, bad dates) is logged exactly as many times as it was injected
- category totals and department totals both add up to the grand total, and every variance equals actual minus budget

CI runs the tests, checks the sample data regenerates byte-for-byte from its seeds, builds the workbook and PDF, and uploads them as a build artifact.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

```sh
npm ci
npm test          # 10 tests
npm run report    # writes output/monthend-YYYY-MM.xlsx and .pdf
npm run generate  # optional: rebuild the synthetic sample data
```

To use your own exports, put the CSV files in a folder and point the script at it:

```sh
node src/run.js --in path/to/exports --budget path/to/budget.csv --vendors path/to/vendors.csv --out reports
```

Exports need the columns `Txn ID, Date, Vendor, Department, Category, Amount, Memo`. The report covers the latest month found, compared with the month before (or pass `--period 2026-10`). Slash dates in `NN/NN/YYYY` form are read as US month/day, matching the sample export's format. A different source would need that setting, and the department and category lists, adjusted in [`src/clean.js`](src/clean.js).

## Layout

```
data/raw/          messy sample exports (generated)
data/budget.csv    monthly budget by department and category
data/vendors.csv   vendor master list (correct spellings)
src/clean.js       parsing, normalising, de-duplicating, issue log
src/summary.js     actual vs budget vs prior month
src/excel.js       workbook writer (exceljs)
src/pdf.js         one-page summary (pdfkit)
src/sample.js      synthetic data generator
test/              reconciliation tests (node:test)
```
